summary: The SSH Diffie-Hellman group exchange says servers and clients should support groups of at least 1024 bits. Recent research showed this is insufficient against well-resourced attackers, so this document raises the minimum recommended modulus size to 2048 bits.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo updates SSH Diffie-Hellman group exchange to recommend groups of at least 2048 bits. It also recommends that clients be able to request a preferred group size of 3072 bits.

subtitle: Raises SSH Diffie-Hellman group size recommendations to at least 2048 bits.

tldr.problem: The SSH group-exchange specification recommended a 1024-bit minimum, which the cited research considered insufficient against well-resourced attackers.
tldr.mechanism: The update recommends SSH clients and servers support groups of at least 2048 bits and clients be able to request a preferred size of 3072 bits.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8270 updates RFC 4419 and recommends minimum group sizes of 2048 bits.

today: RFC 8270 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 4419. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes RFC 8270.

sections.title: Why the Minimum Increased
sections.content: RFC 4419 recommended a minimum Diffie-Hellman modulus size of 1024 bits for SSH group exchange. The research cited by RFC 8270 showed how 768-bit groups could be broken and extrapolated that attack to 1024-bit groups, given sufficient computing resources. This memo updates the recommended minimum to 2048 bits.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier SSH recommendation allowed 1024-bit groups. The cited research led this memo to recommend larger groups.

sections.title: Group Size Recommendations
sections.content:
SSH servers and clients SHOULD support groups with a modulus length from 2048 through 8192 bits. The recommended minimum and maximum values are 2048 and 8192, and setting the group size to 3072 SHOULD be possible. In all cases, the group SHOULD be at least 2048 bits.

Clients SHOULD be able to send 3072 as the preferred acceptable size in the group-exchange request. The RFC says a minimum of 3072 bits may be appropriate for forward-looking users.
sections.plainLanguage: Servers and clients should support groups from 2048 to 8192 bits. Clients should also be able to request 3072 bits as their preferred size.

sections.title: Selecting a Group
sections.content: The server should return the smallest group it knows that is larger than the size requested by the client. If it knows no group larger than the request, it SHOULD return the largest group it knows. The returned group SHOULD be at least 2048 bits, and setting the group size to 3072 SHOULD be possible.
sections.plainLanguage: The server chooses the smallest group it has that exceeds the requested size. The returned group should still meet the 2048-bit minimum recommendation.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC warns that a hostile SSH server could provide backdoored Diffie-Hellman primes or send a calculated secret through a covert channel. A malicious client could also cause denial of service by making repeated connections using groups smaller than 2048 bits. Operating systems SHOULD NOT log groups smaller than 2048 bits because doing so would create an additional attack surface.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC describes risks from a hostile server and from repeated small-group requests. It recommends that operating systems not log groups below the stated size.
